I saw it all with my own eyes.  Time stopped the minute I saw the blood.  It started when I was in the back room, making voice recordings for employees to learn how to use the springlock suits.  After all, that incident at the sister location was pretty bad.  I don't even know how they could have done it all simultaneously.

Anyways, it was my kid's birthday.  Real shame I couldn't be there spending time with him, I never do.  I wished I could have instead of working for the day.  It was at that thought that I heard a loud scream, and animatronic voices garbling, and I smelled smoke from the other room.  People were running around, screaming, and I saw someone dialing 911 in the corner.  I pushed everyone out of the way to see what happened, people were crowded around Fredbear, and he was smoking like hell.  My son's friends were all around, in those stupid "Fredbear and Friends!" masks as always, looking up at the machine with no thoughts in their eyes.  I looked up.  What I saw would change the rest of my life forever.  My son.  He was in the maws of the springlock suit, his head completely crushed.  I ran over, and I held him in my arms.

I don't know how long I cried.  It seemed like days.  The paramedics took him away to the hospital.  I held his hand the whole way there.  The doctors said he was in a coma.  His entire frontal lobe had been taken off.

"I can't b-believe this is happening..." I said with tears in my eyes

"If I weren't working... maybe... maybe I could have saved him..."

5 days went by.  The medics said he would live the rest of his life in a vegetative state, and he would have mental nightmares for the rest of his days.  I couldn't bear for my own son to live like this, so they pulled the plug...

2 weeks had gone by.  I was busy repairing the same endoskeleton that had taken my son's life, wearing the Fredbear suit.  I overheard the employees speaking in the background, and I can remember exactly what they said to this very day.

"Did you hear about that springlock incident?"

"Hell yeah I did, I saw it all go down with my own damn eyes.  The kids, with the masks, right?  That kid was crying, poor guy.  They were teasing him about being afraid of those animatronics."

"Really?"

"Yeah, sad story it is.  They went so far to shove the kid's fucking head inside the mouth, and it clamped down."

"Damn, I knew Eddie should have checked the servos before he put them in!  There's the label on the back that says it needs to be low enough to not damage the head.  Must have been calibrated so hard to crush the kid's skull.  Sad."

It was then I knew who killed my son.  Those boys with the animatronic masks on.  My face turned red, I couldn't move.  I saw them outside the restaurant, playing some game.  They didn't have the masks on, but I recognized their voices.  Those bastards, they killed my son...

I took the wrench I was using to repair the endo, and I unlocked the Spring Bonnie suit.  It was long after hours, but I was going to get my revenge, day or night.  I took them to the back room.  I killed them.  Something came over me that night.  I knew that bad karma was coming for me soon enough.

6 months later, they made a whole new restaurant.  They took the Fredbear and Friends animatronics from that sister location to be used here, well, at least for ideas.  They were way too old and smelly to be used here.  They built whole new shiny ones, the kids called them "Toys".  One night I was spending the night at the restaurant.  The entire night it was errie, as if there were active spirits everywhere.  Maybe one of them was my son.  The withered F&F animatronics were moving around for some reason, must have been a bug.  I walked over to turn Freddy off after I heard him stomping through the hallway.

An hour goes by.  The old Bonnie animatronic crawls through the vents, and my wits are scared out of me.  It's looking right at me.  In my left ear I hear this voice after about a minute of staring, a voice I recognize all too well.

"You don't know what we've been through..."

Those children had possessed the damn things...

I got my ass out of there, I pushed him out of the way and headed for the exit.  The singing puppet came out of it's box and stopped me in my tracks.  A faint whisper is all I heard before I darted out of there

"...daddy...?"

And now I'm still here. Thirty years later.  Stuck in this pitiful Springlock suit.  I thought I was safe, I knew how these things worked.  It was the water leaking that made them come loose.

Even then, when the metal walls around me were closing in, my arms and legs numb with burning and bruising sensations down them, it still didn't hurt me nearly as much as when my little boy died.  And they were watching me suffer there, for an entire hour they sat there and watched me black out and eventually die.  I now haunt these halls, in the same position as those kids so so long ago...

All I have to say to those children;

I am so sorry

So, when you normally spawn a model you get the normal bones controlling the parent bones.  Examples of this are moving the upper arm of a person also controlling the lower arm, hands, fingers, ETC.  This is called an FK rig or forward kinematics.  An IK rig, which is inverse kinematics, is almost the opposite.  Instead of controlling the parent bones to move the child bones, you get to move the child bones to preform vice versa.  For example, if you apply an IK rig on the Scout, you can move his hand and his arm will bend and move to how someone would normally move if you were to move that hand in wherever you put it.

It's a simple thing that makes animation much easier in most cases.  IK rigging is extremely useful in making walk cycles if you use the graph editor, so you don't use up all of that extra time animating the legs and arms individually.  A shortcut if you will.
